clue.text: Unbeliever me, suspicious fiend ending in hell

parts.note: the speaker, me, is I

indicators.note: suspicious suggests something fishy, so the word fiend is cooked into a new order
ending in points to the final letter of the word hell

explanation.surface: A believer recoils at a devilish figure who is bound for hell and is suspicious of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspicious' looks like a description of the fiend, but it is the anagram signal; 'ending in' takes only the last letter of 'hell'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone with no religious faith, especially from another creed's point of view, is an infidel.

clue.text: Tell man from Belfast to stand?

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means the words are read upwards

parts.note: Mr is the title for a man
of can mean from, as in coming of good family
Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, NI

explanation.surface: Someone asks a Northern Irishman to stand up and speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man from Belfast' reads as MR OF NI, a title, 'of' and Northern Ireland; 'to stand' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to inform someone is to tell them a fact.

clue.text: Loose skin punctured by bees, we hear?

indicators.note: punctured by says the second element pierces the first and sits inside it

parts.note: to flay is to strip off the skin

indicators.note: we hear marks a sound-alike: the insects become letters

parts.note: bees sounds like two letter Bs

explanation.surface: Someone's sagging skin gets stung by a swarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin' is the verb, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: flesh that hangs slack and soft is loose.

clue.text: Abroad, I start to eat angel cakes for tea

indicators.note: cakes in the sense of coats or encrusts, so the endearment goes round the other letters

parts.note: angel and darling are terms of endearment
je is French for I

indicators.note: start to points to the first letter of the word eat

explanation.surface: On holiday overseas, someone tucks into angel cakes with their tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angel cakes' looks like a sponge, but 'angel' is a term of endearment and 'cakes' is a verb, to coat, so it wraps round the other letters. 'Abroad' makes I French.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fine black variety grown in the Indian hills near the Himalayas is a type of tea.

clue.text: Drink less bubbly, taking lips away

indicators.note: lips are the edges, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: a drink with less fizz is flatter

explanation.surface: A drink loses its fizz while someone sips it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking lips away' strips F and R from the ends of FLATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a coffee made with lots of steamed milk is a drink.

clue.text: Tool had been picked out by journalist?

indicators.note: by puts the journalist as the one doing the seeing, so that word comes first

parts.note: a hack is slang for a run-of-the-mill journalist
picked out in the sense of spotted, which is what one saw

explanation.surface: A tool has been spotted and singled out by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'had been picked out by journalist' as 'the journalist saw it': HACK then SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fine-toothed saw for cutting metal is one kind of tool.

clue.text: Cold about right?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cold word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: something cold has no warmth, it is heatless

explanation.surface: A question whether a chilly estimate is near the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' does double duty, as definition and as the word around R. 'about right' wants to mean roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unfeeling, cruel person is called cold, without compassion or warmth.

clue.text: See 19
Previous excerpt from poem, item ostensibly uplifting

indicators.note: uplifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
an excerpt is a passage lifted out, so the letters come from inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cheerful excerpt from a poem, apparently a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Previous excerpt' as the definition; 'excerpt from' is the hidden-word signal, leaving 'Previous'. Upward in a down clue, the letters in poEM ITEM OStensibly read SOMETIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: former or one-time, as in a sometime professor, means previous.

clue.text: Caribbean islands where snake gets protection

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a road does
ward means guardianship or protection

explanation.surface: On some Caribbean islands, snakes are a protected species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake' is the verb, to twist about.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: the southern Lesser Antilles, Grenada to Dominica, are called the Windward Islands.

clue.text: Reportedly burn gift

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear the word rather than see it written

parts.note: to flare is to burn brightly

explanation.surface: A news report claims some burn was handed over as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a natural talent or knack is a gift.

clue.text: Business people, a number getting to grips with shattered dreams

indicators.note: to get to grips with is to grasp, so the number holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: shattered dreams are broken into pieces, so that word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some entrepreneurs see their dreams in ruins and try to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' is the anagram signal on dreams; 'getting to grips with' makes the number hold those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shopkeepers and skilled workers who trade goods or services are business people.

clue.text: To cover debts, pinch my wages from safe

parts.note: to pinch is to steal, rob
peter is old criminal slang for a safe
the setter is Paul, so his wages are money to pay him

explanation.surface: Someone in debt takes the setter's salary out of the safe to settle up.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter signs himself Paul, so 'my wages' is money TO PAY PAUL; 'from' is a link word in the wordplay. PETER is old crooks' slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: settling one debt by running up another, borrowing from one person to repay another.

clue.text: Pull something that's nailed, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks whether we heard the word, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a toe carries a toenail

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they misheard a request to pull out something nailed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nailed' suggests carpentry, but it means having a nail on it, as a toe does.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to drag a vehicle or boat behind on a rope is to pull it.

clue.text: Fifty shells initially loading rocket launchers, hope that makes you breathe easier

indicators.note: loading means the other letters are added as cargo straight after the space agency

parts.note: NASA, the US space agency, launches rockets
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word shells

parts.note: to pray is to hope earnestly

explanation.surface: A space mission loads up shells and hopes for a calm launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocket launchers' is the US space agency, not weapons; 'loading' just adds the following letters onto it.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a squirted decongestant mist clears blocked nostrils, helping you breathe.

clue.text: Bound to get hard in prison, this employed with force!

indicators.note: in places the boundary and the hard letter within the prison

parts.note: the slammer is slang for prison
a bound is a boundary or edge
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A prisoner sentenced to hard labour swings a heavy tool with great force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like a verb (leap or tie) but is a noun, a boundary. The definition plays on breaking rocks in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a heavy long-handled hammer is the tool swung with force, as once in prison rock-breaking.

clue.text: I'd sent off essay, painful work?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A student posted off a gruelling essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges I'D SENT to DENTIS; 'essay' is the attempt, not the composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Joke: work on teeth, the trade of a tooth doctor, can be painful for the patient.

clue.text: Third of colony, a thousand sat together

indicators.note: third of takes the opening third, two of the six letters, of the word colony

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a model sat or posed for a painter

explanation.surface: A third of a colony, a thousand in all, sat down together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third of colony' is its first third, CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone calm and self-possessed is together, in the informal sense.

clue.text: Gaze round capitals of Egypt and Morocco with glasses?

indicators.note: round says the gaze goes about the other letters

parts.note: to gaze is to stare

indicators.note: capitals of points to the initial letters of the words Egypt and Morocco

explanation.surface: A traveller stares about North African capitals wearing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' wants Cairo and Rabat but means initial letters. 'glasses' are drinking glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Category: wine glasses and goblets with stems are collectively called this.

clue.text: Revealed where stud may be ditched unceremoniously

parts.note: a secret that is revealed is out
an earring stud sits in a pierced lobe, on the wearer's ear

explanation.surface: An earring stud is spotted, then thrown away without ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being thrown out bluntly, dismissed without ceremony, is to be out on your ear.

clue.text: Restraint maintained by pro sent up in novel

indicators.note: maintained by says the restraint is held inside the other letters
in a down clue, sent up means read upwards

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a manacle is a shackle, a restraint

explanation.surface: A captive held by a professional is ridiculed in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns FOR to ROF, holding MANACLE. 'pro' is not professional but for.
explanation.definitionFit: Category: a French term for fiction portraying real people under invented names, a kind of novel.

clue.text: Ship in a bottle, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a boat or craft at sea
a container for liquid, such as a bottle

explanation.surface: A model ship sits inside a glass bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a large boat, and any hollow container for holding liquid.

clue.text: Victoria's Englishman, hair combed back

indicators.note: combed back says the hair word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a mop is a shaggy head of hair

explanation.surface: An Englishman in Melbourne has his hair slicked back.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is not the queen but the Australian state, so the definition wants Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: Australians, as in the state of Victoria, call a Briton a pom or pommy.

clue.text: Result of sin clear when screwed

indicators.note: screwed means twisted up, so the letters are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about what comes of sinning when having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the last tally of points at the end of a match is the result.

clue.text: Every other part of tale is so apt for storyteller

indicators.note: every other part takes alternate letters of the words tale is so apt

explanation.surface: A storyteller's tale is said to be apt in part.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the ancient Greek fabulist behind the hare and tortoise was a famous storyteller.

clue.text: Girl going up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue the name reads the same going up as going down

parts.note: A girl's name, spelt the same in either direction

explanation.surface: A girl rides a lift or seesaw up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: a common female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Rump of venison possibly festers

parts.note: venison is deer meat, and a stag is one source of it
nates is the anatomical word for the buttocks

explanation.surface: A haunch of deer meat left out goes off and rots.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'Rump of venison' first, but in the answer the deer comes before the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that festers is left to rot and stagnates, without movement or freshening.

clue.text: Transport network for island under discussion

indicators.note: something under discussion is spoken about, so its sound matters

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A Greek island's transport network is being debated.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: highways and streets together form a network for transport.

clue.text: Looking at regular intake, conclusions of the provost scheduled, it's suggested?

indicators.note: to schedule is to enter in a diary, so the end letters are written inside it

parts.note: a diary entry suggests a thing is booked in, so the diary is what the phrase hints at

indicators.note: conclusions of points to the end letters of the words the and provost

explanation.surface: A college head's regular food intake is being reviewed on a schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scheduled' is the container signal: the provost's conclusions are written into the diary that 'it's suggested' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: anything concerning what one regularly eats, one's diet, is dietary.

clue.text: See 11
